Subject: Recap + next steps — Performance SLO (p95/p99) qualification

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the time today — great discussion. Per our call, I wanted to capture the key items and proposed next steps so we can validate whether Redwood Hosted hits Finlytics' end-to-end latency SLOs.

TL;DR (ask): Finlytics is aiming for an end-to-end p95 <= 500ms and p99 <= 1.5s for the primary text-generation route (including network and any client-side latency). You mentioned current provider numbers (roughly p95 ~450ms, p99 ~1.2s) and those are the baseline we should beat or match.

What we discussed (short):
- Workload profile: median prompt ~120 tokens, response payload ~220 tokens on average, occasional large (>1k token) batched jobs.
- Concurrency/throughput: steady-state concurrency ~30–50 concurrent requests, peak bursts to ~120 concurrent for <2 minutes.
- Streaming: partial/streaming responses required for product UX (token-by-token delivery).
- Important SLO semantics: Finlytics measures p95/p99 end-to-end from user request to first token visible (for streaming) and to final token for non-streaming routes.

Data we need from Finlytics: (if you can share before our tech call)
1) Real client-side traces (one busy hour, UTC timestamps) showing p95/p99 measurements.
2) Representative sample of prompt/response payloads (sanitized).
3) Typical QPS and concurrency over 24h (CSV or spreadsheet).

What Redwood will provide before the technical deep dive:
- A short benchmarking plan and scripts we can run against your staging workload.
- Expected hosted API latency profile for a comparable model (p95/p99 targets and token-level timings).
- A short SLO matrix (attached) mapping observed load to recommended config (batching, concurrency caps, streaming mode).

Next steps:
- Alex/Priya: Share traces and the CSV export for last 24h (ask above) by Tue 6/23 if possible.
- We'll schedule a 45-min tech deep-dive the week of 6/23 — include Aditya (serving/runtime) and Dylan (SRE).
- I'll attach the SLO matrix + a short latency report baseline.

Thanks — happy to adjust timing if you need more time to pull traces.

Best,

Thanks for looping us in — quick read and a few notes from the serving/runtime perspective before the deep-dive:

1) Clarify measurement points: Finlytics measures to first token for streaming — correct. That means we need to optimize both network path and token generation latency. End-to-end p95 <= 500ms is achievable in many cases, but depends heavily on:
   - model variant and quantization profile (FP16 vs 4-bit quantized),
   - client-to-edge network RTT (if they are regionally far from our region),
   - request batching settings and concurrency throttles.

2) Quick numbers (ballpark based on similar customers):
   - Hosted (typical open/model mid-sized): p95 ~180–280ms, p99 ~420–650ms (to first token) under steady concurrency 20–60 with streaming enabled and our small-window kv cache.
   - Under bursty concurrency (100+), p99 can spike unless we apply concurrency caps and prioritized lanes — we should present a plan for graceful degradation.

3) Action items for technical call:
   - Get one hour of representative traces (client->edge->api->model->client) and a sample of the exact prompt/response sizes.
   - Confirm target model variant (we can run a lab test against an equivalent open model).
   - We'll prepare a quick runbook: test scenarios (steady QPS, burst ramp, large-batch), expected config changes (batch size, request_coalescing window), and an A/B comparison chart vs their current provider.

I attached a short latency diagram (p95_p99_latency_diagram.png) that explains how we measure first-token vs end-to-end final-token.
